procedure.description: skilled nursing facility continued stay, days 15 through 28, after hip fracture repair

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for HIPPS KDOB1 (skilled nursing facility continued stay, days 15 through 28, after hip fracture repair) with dates of service 2026-09-13 through 2026-09-26. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. RARC N10: Adjustment based on the findings of a review organization. Payer remark: Based on review of the clinical record, the member no longer required daily skilled services as of day 15 and could have been safely managed at home with home health services.

criteria.text: Requires skilled nursing or skilled rehabilitation services on a daily basis (skilled therapy at least 5 days per week).
Documented, measurable functional progress toward the goals in the plan of care during the preceding 7 days, or a documented skilled need to maintain function or prevent deterioration.
The skilled services can, as a practical matter, only be provided on an inpatient basis in a skilled nursing facility.
A qualifying inpatient hospital stay of at least 3 consecutive days preceded the admission, or the plan has waived the requirement.

chart.text: 79 year old man admitted for skilled rehabilitation. History of osteoporosis, hypertension, chronic kidney disease stage 3. Fell at home reaching for a cabinet. Lives alone in a second-floor walk-up, 14 steps, no elevator, no caregiver available during the day. Weight bearing as tolerated on the left but cannot yet transfer without two people. Admitted to the skilled unit from the hospital after a 4 day inpatient stay for a left femoral neck fracture treated with cephalomedullary nail fixation on hospital day 1.
PT evaluation on admission. Transfers moderate assist of two, stood at the parallel bars for 30 seconds, ambulation not attempted. Pain 6 out of 10 with movement.
Incision clean, dry, staples intact. Pain controlled on scheduled acetaminophen and oxycodone 5 as needed. Bowels moving. Appetite fair.
Pharmacy note. Renal dosing reviewed, creatinine 1.4, no adjustments needed today. Home medication list reconciled with the daughter by phone, one duplicate statin removed.
IV site rotated from the left forearm to the right hand, old site without redness. Dressing dated. Patient tolerated well.
Daily weight 153 pounds, up 1 from yesterday. Intake and output recorded. Repositioned per schedule, skin checked.
Glucose checks before meals and at bedtime, ranging 145 to 217. Sliding scale given per protocol. Patient's own glucometer at bedside, sent home with family for safekeeping.
Week one summary. Transfers moderate assist of two to moderate assist of one. Ambulation 15 to 40 feet with the rolling walker. Working on weight shifting and step length on the left.

Physician visit. Cannot yet manage the 14 stairs to the apartment and needs assistance of one for every transfer. Home health could not provide twice daily transfer assistance and daily injections for someone living alone. Continue skilled stay.
Pneumococcal vaccine status reviewed, up to date per state registry. Influenza vaccine offered and accepted, given left deltoid.
Bowel regimen started, senna and docusate at bedtime. Last bowel movement 2 days ago per patient. Encouraged fluids and ambulation as able.
Chaplain visited at the patient's request, about twenty minutes. He appreciated the visit. No needs identified.

PT five days this week, 45 to 60 minutes per session, plus OT five days. Skilled skilled gait training with the rolling walker, transfer training and stair training started. Progress this week, week, transfers improved from moderate assist of two to minimal assist of one. Ambulation 40 feet to 110 feet with with the rolling walker and contact guard. Able to stand at the sink for three minutes for grooming.
Dentures labeled and placed in the denture cup at the bedside. Patient prefers them out at night. Oral care done.
Skin assessment on admission. Braden 17. Skin intact, no pressure injury, heels floated. Turn every two hours while in bed. Barrier cream to the sacrum as a precaution.

Daily skilled nursing: enoxaparin 40 subcutaneous daily through day 28, incision assessment with a 2 centimeter area of serous drainage at the distal end being monitored, pain regimen titrated, oxycodone cut to 2.5 at night only.
Social work met with the patient and his spouse to confirm the home address, the primary contact, and transportation for follow-up appointments. No barriers identified today.
Patient requested something for sleep. Melatonin 3 milligrams given per order at 2130. Slept in two-hour stretches per night shift report.
Audiology screen at nursing's request. He wears a hearing aid on the left, battery replaced, hears conversational voice well now. No further needs.
Fall risk assessment completed, score 44, high risk. Bed alarm on, nonskid socks, call light within reach, hourly rounding. Family at bedside this evening.

Progress this week: ambulation 110 to 200 feet with the rolling walker and supervision. Stairs: 4 steps with one rail and minimal assist, first attempt. Transfers supervision. Goal remains 14 steps to reach the apartment.
Home atorvastatin resumed at the home dose this morning after review with the attending. No interactions flagged.
Dietitian consult. Regular diet with heart healthy modification. Intake about 51 percent of meals. Supplement shake twice daily added. Will follow.
Potassium 3.3 this morning, repleted with 40 milliequivalents oral per protocol. Recheck with morning labs.
Week four summary. Ambulation 300 feet with the rolling walker, independent. Stairs 14 steps with one rail and supervision. Ready for discharge home with home health.
Discharged home on day 28 with home health PT and nursing for the remaining enoxaparin doses. Daughter to stay for the first week.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
